content.thinking:
I'm checking the API details—whether decal placement supports points with direction, multi-segment arrays, and whether scaling a unit sphere part works correctly for ellipsoid shapes once rotated into place. I also want to confirm that surface and decal functions accept Part objects as input.

For eyes, I can treat `at` as a ray origin set slightly outward from the skull surface along the direction vector, so the decal projects back onto the head without needing an actual hit test. I'm computing the outward direction using the azimuth angle (62°, 22° elevation) to get the eye position, then offsetting along that vector by a small amount for `at`. I need to double check whether mirroring highlight positions for both eyes would look visually off, since both might end up positioned the same way in screen space rather than mirrored.

For the ears, I'm defining a teardrop-shaped outline with five points and smoothing applied, extruded along the side axis with bevel and bone attachment. For the body, I'm deciding between faceted (low sides count, no smoothing) versus smooth shading, leaning toward a faceted look with around 10 sides to match a blocky puppet aesthetic consistent with the rest of the model.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building sphere-based ellipsoid parts with configurable radii, color, position, and bone attachment, then starting to write the module imports and color palette constants for the fur tones, nose colors, and other materials needed for the character.

I'm continuing the color palette, adding tones for the bird's beak, feathers, blush, and legs, plus a separate palette for daisy petals and centers.

For eyes and small details, I'm planning to use decal textures on spherical geometry instead of flat cards, keeping the overall texture count manageable within a target range.

I'll settle on the decal set: eye, bird eye, mouth, blush, tufts, and a feather pattern decal for the wing surface to add detail without extra geometry. Now I'm thinking through the bird's coloring, using a vertical gradient paint function that shifts from blue on top to cream on the belly based on surface normal direction.

For texel density I'm figuring out the atlas resolution needed to keep consistent detail across both the capybara and bird parts without over-allocating space.

Now I'm starting to build the capybara skeleton, defining the hip joint as the root of the spine hierarchy.

Still building the skeleton...

Tail stub sweeps from the rump cap down and back with two short segments, dark fur color, parented to the hips with names "tail1" and "tail2".

Now I'm sketching the legs: computing shoulder and foot positions based on the body's center and radius, picking segment lengths around 0.12-0.13 so the leg spans from the body down to near the floor, and double-checking which sign of the lateral offset corresponds to left versus right in my coordinate loop.

For the hind legs, I'm setting root and target points with similar offsets, choosing segment lengths so the total distance leaves room for a bend, and assigning bend-hint directions -- back for the front elbow, forward for the hind knee -- matching the three-point chain convention for each limb. I'm also starting to define tapering radii for the thigh segments.

Now I'm attaching leg chains to the appropriate spine segments based on front/hind position, placing foot ellipsoids at the leg tips, and spacing toe geometry evenly across each foot.

The leg's rounded cap could poke below the floor, so I'm adjusting the target leg-bottom y to 0.055 to keep it within tolerance, and checking the foot ellipsoid lands right at ground level. Leg length and body height still line up fine with these adjustments, so now I'm moving on to sizing the hind haunch ellipsoid.

Checking the haunch's position against the body's half-width at that z-depth, it fits with a slight bulge outward, so that's fine. I'm sketching out the shoulder ellipsoid dimensions next, then setting up the body sweep along the spine chain and the neck sweep, though I notice the neck sweep's rounded end cap might extend slightly past the intended endpoint and need adjustment.

Now I'm placing the head components: the skull ellipsoid, the cheek ellipsoids on either side, and a frustum-box snout tapering forward with a slight downward tilt. I'm positioning the nose bump at the front of the snout and checking that its vertical placement aligns correctly with the snout's top surface.

Adding a small highlight ellipsoid on top of the nose for shine, then placing nostril sticks using surface-normal positioning on the nose geometry, working out the right small scale values for them.

Now I'm sketching a helper to safely get hit points on the surface without crashing on null results. For the jaw, I'm building a frustum box shape with a lighter chin section and adding a small chin tuft ellipsoid, then starting on tooth geometry as small boxes positioned along the jawline.

Now I'm placing a mouth decal on the snout's front face, checking that the nose bump above it won't visually obstruct the mouth since their y-ranges barely overlap, and double-checking the snout box's tilt to make sure the decal's ray direction actually lands on the right surface.

I'm skipping eyebrow details for simplicity, finalizing the ears via extrusion with inner detail on both sides, and now setting up whiskers as small groups of base-to-tip line segments positioned along the snout.

For body fur, I'm planning scattered card elements across surface hit points with a leaning, bending flow directed back and down to give a natural coat texture, and thinking about whether legs need similar treatment.

For fur density, I'm sketching out roughly 260 cards on the body filtered to avoid the belly, plus around 70 on the cheeks and skull avoiding areas near the top where the beak sits, tinted with the coat color and following the same back-and-down lean.

Thinking about details like a small snout bump mimicking a capybara's scent gland, then moving to building the bird: setting its base position and orientation so it faces slightly toward the viewer at a gentle angle for a cute three-quarter view, and starting a helper function for placing bird body points.

Now I'm working out joint placement for the bird's body, head, beak, and wings, figuring out parent-child relationships and roles for each joint so the rig articulates naturally.

For the head and body, since the bird is yawed, I need to apply a rotation to the ellipsoid so its axes align with the yaw angle rather than staying fixed to the model's world axes. I'm placing the head ellipsoid above the body, checking that the vertical positions don't cause unwanted overlap between the head and the top of the body.

Now I'm sketching out the beak as a pair of spikes (upper and lower) attached to bones for the head and lower jaw, plus adding eye decals positioned slightly offset to each side of the head.

For the eye texture I'm designing a simple black eye with a glint and tiny lash line using an SVG viewBox. I'm also considering how to add cheek blush, debating between a decal approach or a dedicated blush part on the head.

Now I'm figuring out blush placement using a flattened stick shape oriented to the surface normal, and setting up the wings as backward-sloping ellipsoids with their own position and scale along the model's local axes.

Setting decal up direction to point from tip toward root with feathers pointing down, sizing it roughly to the wing length even though it's a rough approximation. I'm wary of overcomplicating things, so I might skip the wing decal entirely and instead build feathers from layered ellipsoids.

Actually I'll add three thin rod-shaped flight feathers fanning from the wing's rear tip, colored dark blue with cream tips, computing each one's start and end points by rotating a base direction vector slightly around the bird's up axis.

Writing feather sweep code...

Shaping the crest feathers to curl forward playfully, with the central feather taller than the sides. I'm considering whimsical extras like floating hearts but deciding against overcomplicating the beak area.

Now I'm positioning a small daisy decal near the skull, checking angular spacing so it doesn't overlap the eye or ear decals—working out the clearance margins between each feature.

Writing petal ring code...

Setting the center embed amount, then considering whether to add small green leaves near the flower and a bird perched on top, though I decide to skip some optional details for simplicity. I'm double-checking ground contact so the feet and tail sit correctly at y near zero.

I'm sketching a tuft texture with a grey-to-white gradient leaf blade, then designing the mouth SVG with dark brown rounded strokes, a philtrum, and small cheek dimples sized to raster cleanly at 512px.

Now I'm building the eye SVG with a clipped iris structure: a dark outer ellipse, a warm brown mid-layer, a glowing lower highlight, and a near-black pupil, plus an eyelid path shaping the top curve.

Checking the clip boundary math confirms the lid stroke stays within the ellipse bounds. For the blush, I'm sketching a pink oval with a few darker streaks to suggest cheek shading, adjusting the color to a softer coral tone that fits the whimsical style better.

For the bird eye, a simple black ellipse with glint highlights should work fine within the viewBox, and I'll skip adding extra hair tufts since triangle budget is tight. Now I'm defining the COAT paint function, layering fur color gradients based on surface normal direction and blending in noise-driven streaks for a mottled, textured look.

Writing fur texture noise...

Then I'm sketching out the bird's paint function, blending cream for the belly against blue tones for the back, with a lighter blue highlight gradient based on the normal's y-component to simulate light catching the top of the bird.

Writing ellipsoid helper function...

Still working out the sphere helper's typing...

Setting up the leg loop for both sides, defining front limb joints with hip, foot, and bend direction parameters to build each chain.

For toe placement I'll use the foot chain's joint reference directly. Now I'm checking eye placement relative to the skull geometry — computing the eye direction vector and target offset from the head center, then worrying whether the cheek ellipsoid pokes above the skull surface near where the eye decal sits, since their radii and positions seem to overlap.

I work out the overlap numerically: the eye decal's lower edge dips into the cheek bulge, so I adjust by lowering the cheek center and shrinking its radius, plus tightening the eye decal height and nudging its vertical position up slightly to compensate. Then I check the snout box width against the skull's half-width at the same z-depth and notice it extends past the skull boundary there.

Checking the snout box geometry, I see it tapers correctly within the skull until a certain depth, then pokes out intentionally to form the muzzle — matching a dome-forehead-plus-blunt-snout look. Now I'm checking the neck sweep's radius and where its front cap meets the head base.

For the ears, I'm computing hit points on the skull surface at specific azimuth/elevation angles, offsetting slightly inward along the normal to anchor the ear base, then building a simple pointed-oval outline with rounded smoothing for the ear shape before extruding it with some thickness.

Adding inner ear detail...

With body fur cards done, I'm adding a small scatter of tuft cards near the skull top around the bird's nest area, filtered by upward-facing normals and proximity to the perch, to give a nesting feel beneath the bird's feet.

Now I'm setting up helper position and direction functions for the bird parts, applying axis rotation and offset, and defining the bird's joint hierarchy starting with the root bird joint attached to the head.

I'm continuing to define the bird skeleton: the birdHead joint, a beakLower joint with a "jaw" role aimed downward, and left/right wing joints with "wing" roles positioned and aimed outward from the body.

Adding a birdTail joint with a direction vector, then noting that single joints can carry roles directly. I'm setting up body painting with rotation flags and planning wing feather fan directions using axis-angle rotation around the Y axis for a spread effect, then starting the wings loop function.

Writing wings loop...

I need to position the wing just outside the body surface, adjusting the x offset to around .062-.064 so it sits properly against the body's curve. Now I'm adding feather details, spreading a few feather directions outward from the wing base using small angle offsets.

Writing sweep geometry...

Adding crest feather strokes...

The head top aligns with the quadratic sweep positions, confirming geometry fits. I'm also thinking through cheek blush decals on the capybara, positioning them outward on the cheek ellipsoid so they face correctly, and checking whether the scatter cards covering cheeks would overlap or obscure them.

I'll restrict the cheek fur cards to the back and bottom of the cheek by filtering normal directions, keeping them away from the blush area. Skipping whiskers and a scarf idea, I'll add a few extra touches like slight eyebrow ellipsoids, cheek ruff cards, and claws before writing out the final code.

Now I'm defining a smooth keyframe interpolation helper and using it to sweep the body profile radii along the spine, checking the resulting back and head heights to see if the head should sit lower than the back for a more natural capybara silhouette.

I'm shifting the head position down slightly and re-parametrizing the skull, snout, jaw, teeth, mouth decal, cheeks, whiskers, and neck coordinates relative to a single head-center y-value so everything scales together consistently.

Now I'm computing the joint positions for the head and jaw, adjusting the bird's offset to match, and planning the body scatter logic for fur cards with filters based on surface normals and z-position before writing the full file.

For the bird's blush placement, I'm working out the azimuth math relative to its forward direction so the positioning rotates correctly with the head angle.

I still need to sequence the nose/nostril builds before stacking decals on top, and double-check eye spacing and the rotation/axis options for wings before finalizing.

Verifying the sweep function accepts a vector path and radius array correctly, and that the chain contact param works fine with the feet. Good to write now.
